concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a well-defined, hard, nontender swelling in the right buccal vestibule with buccal cortical expansion, a ground-glass trabecular pattern on radiographs, and expansion of the buccal and palatal cortical plates on cone-beam CT is consistent with juvenile ossifying fibroma.
Although less likely due to the well-defined margin of the swelling, fibrous dysplasia is still considered based on the radiographic findings of a ground-glass appearance and cortical expansion.

rationales.F05: The ground-glass trabecular pattern is more typical of juvenile ossifying fibroma.
rationales.F06: Increased radiopacity and a ground-glass appearance are characteristic of juvenile ossifying fibroma.
rationales.F07: The well-defined margin and ground-glass internal pattern are more consistent with juvenile ossifying fibroma.
rationales.F10: The well-defined margin of the swelling is atypical for fibrous dysplasia, which tends to have ill-defined margins.

frontier_selector.rationale: The well-defined margin of the swelling and the ground-glass internal pattern on imaging are more consistent with Juvenile Ossifying Fibroma, whereas Fibrous Dysplasia typically has an ill-defined margin and merges with surrounding areas.
